set.body:
Journey: See. Track: engine.

Outcome
Every accepted release, BIDS or archive, has a small descriptive record that search, the study page and the catalogue read: title, description, creators, keywords, data types, licence and identifiers.

Why
Search today matches only the optional project label. In the running demo the protocol archive could not be found by words that occur in its own description.

Acceptance
1. The record is derived at acceptance from the accepted descriptor: dataset_description.json and README for BIDS, archive_description.json for archives. Missing fields are recorded as missing. The private project label stays separate.
2. One record per accepted release. R1's record is unchanged after R2 is accepted. A rejected candidate has none.
3. A backfill from retained releases gives the same records as live acceptance. Existing release and manifest identifiers do not change.
4. Each field has one of two disclosure levels: shown to anyone who may know the release exists, or shown only with permission to read metadata.
5. The reference and PostgreSQL catalogs agree on a BIDS fixture and on an archive with no scientific index.

Not in scope
Search itself (SEE3). Facets. Full-text indexing beyond what PostgreSQL offers directly.

Start from
- modules/bids/src/main/scala/sanctity/bids/ArchiveInterpreter.scala line 83: the archive fields.
- modules/postgres/src/main/scala/sanctity/postgres/PostgresOrganizationCatalog.scala line 80: the project directory.

Evidence
Lifecycle tests on both catalogs with independently written expected records.
set.title: SEE2: A catalog record for every accepted release (was ARC02)
